svg.title: Cost per part of face milling versus cutting speed with machine cost, tool cost and the economic optimum
svg.text: Cost per part vs. cutting speed – face mill Ø100, 4 faces per crankcase (example: C 728, n 0.25, 1.5 €/min, 26.25 € per edge set)
Machine cost falls with speed, tool cost rises; the total has a FLAT minimum. Two cases of tool-change time t_ch (machine stopped during the change).
cost per crankcase, face milling share (€)
T_econ = (1/n − 1)(t_ch + K_t / c_M) = 3 · (0.5 + 17.5) = 54 min; T_prod = (1/n − 1) · t_ch = 1.5 min (outside the tested range – not usable).
Check limits before you speed up: spindle power (57 % at ap 2 mm), Taylor validity range, surface finish, chipping of the casting skin.
